checks.claim: Raising the voltage on a transmission line lowers the power lost as heat in the wire.
checks.why: For the same power, higher voltage means lower current, and resistive loss goes with the square of the current (I squared R): double the voltage, a quarter of the loss.

checks.claim: A pole transformer steps the street's voltage down to the 120 and 240 volts used in homes.
checks.why: Pole-mounted distribution transformers take about 7.2 to 34.5 kV and reduce it to split-phase 120/240 V for homes.

checks.claim: Underground power lines are less exposed to wind and falling trees than overhead lines.
checks.why: Utilities say buried lines are less susceptible to wind and falling trees, but they are exposed to flooding and storm surge, so 'far less exposed to storm damage' overstates it.

checks.claim: A circuit breaker trips to cut the power when a circuit is overloaded.
checks.why: Overcurrent devices protect conductors from overheating; a sustained overload heats the breaker's bimetal strip and trips it.

sources.title: EEPower: What are overcurrent protection devices
